title: Perkins: five degrees from Gospel knowledge to special Spirit-persuasion
source_text: XXX. Perkinsius in ortu fidei quinque gradus observat. Primus est notitia Evangelii per illuminationem Spiritus Sancti; quam sequitur in illuminatis omnibus fides generalis, qua praebent assensum Evangelio: Secundus est spes veniae, qua peccator, etsi nondum sentit remissum esse peccatum, remissibile tamen esse credit: Tertius est esuries & vehemens expetitio gratiae, quae est oblata in Christo Jesu: Quartus, accessus ad thronum gratiae, ut apprehenso ibidem Christo, inveniamus misericordiam apud Deum: Quintus est specialis persuasio cordi a Spiritu Sancto impressa, qua promissiones Evangelicas quisque sibi speciatim applicat. In Armilla Aurea, cap. 16.
pass_a_gloss: Perkins observes five degrees in the rise of faith. The first is knowledge of the Gospel by the illumination of the Holy Spirit; which is followed in all the illuminated by a general faith by which they give assent to the Gospel: The second is hope of pardon, by which the sinner, although he does not yet feel that sin has been remitted, yet believes it to be remissible: The third is hunger and vehement desire for the grace which is offered in Christ Jesus: The fourth, access to the throne of grace, that having apprehended Christ there we may find mercy with God: The fifth is a special persuasion impressed on the heart by the Holy Spirit, by which each applies the Evangelical promises to himself specially. In the Golden Chain, chapter 16.
pass_b_english: Perkins (Golden Chain 16): five degrees in faith’s rise.
2. Hope of pardon — remissible even if not yet felt remitted.
3. Hunger for grace offered in Christ.
4. Access to the throne of grace — apprehend Christ; find mercy.
5. Spirit-impressed special persuasion applying Gospel promises to myself.
